summary: Backend-only iter158 verifying new shared-MAC + nic_changed semantics in /app/backend/mac_follow.py and /app/backend/mac_rescue.py. Both existing suites executed with backend .env exported: test_mac_follow_iter154.py PASS 13/13 (covers: TP-Link fingerprint, exclusive MAC follow + rekey, idempotency, conflict skip, follow_mac=False, MAC on 2 IPs skip, first-bind IP assignment, resolve_ip_from_discovery, shared MAC among 3 managed devices with no move/merge/alert and auto-resolution of old mac_follow_multi_ip alerts, exclusive MAC on 2 IPs no-op, nic_changed 2-detection confirmation with HIGH severity for vital, transient ARP + non-vital medium + other managed MAC ignored, mac_is_shared helper). test_mac_rescue_iter159.py PASS 3/3 (start rescue + cooldown + /24 scan, found MAC on new IP triggers HIGH VITALE IP cambiato alert + resolves false offline, not-found closes state). GET /api/health = 200 on public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. All DB test data cleaned up by tests themselves (test-macfollow-* / test-rescue-* client_ids).
critical_code_review_comments: mac_follow._check_nic_change: condition `not seen.get(new_mac, set()) <= group_ips` requires the new MAC to be seen *only* on group IPs; if the agent reports the new MAC on an unrelated managed IP in the same batch (legitimate NIC swap case where the new MAC was briefly seen elsewhere via ARP noise) the alert is suppressed. Documented behavior but might silently miss a real swap in large batches - consider widening check or logging a debug line.

mac_follow.apply_mac_follow: owners dict uses norm_mac but still queries managed_devices with both lowercase and uppercase MAC variants only in mac_is_shared / resolve_ip_from_discovery - any legacy records with mixed case may be excluded from the primary find on line 168-172 (relies on $nin empty-string filter only). Low risk since norm_mac stores lowercase.
NIC_CONFIRM_COUNT=2 and RESCUE_WAIT_S/RESCUE_COOLDOWN_S are module-level constants - consider centralising in a config module if ops needs to tune per-client.
mac_rescue.start_mac_rescue hardcodes /24 subnet; multi-subnet or /23 networks won't be scanned fully. Acceptable for current scope but should be documented.
test_credentials: admin info@86bit.it + 2FA TOTP in /app/memory/test_credentials.md (not used in this iteration; tests hit MongoDB directly, no login required).
seed_data_creation: None. Tests create isolated client_ids (test-macfollow-<hex>, test-rescue-<hex>) and clean up in finally blocks across managed_devices, device_credentials, port_memory, alerts, discovered_endpoints, vital_offline_state, lan_scan_runs, mac_rescue_state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Current semantics (post iter158): shared MAC (same MAC on >1 managed device OR exclusive MAC seen on >1 IP) => no move, no merge/delete, no mac_follow_multi_ip alert; prior active mac_follow_multi_ip alerts auto-resolved via _resolve_shared_noise. Exclusive MAC on a single new unmanaged IP: IP follow applies (rekey + alert mac_follow_ip_update, high for vital/mac_rescue source, medium otherwise, low for first-bind 'IP rilevato'). nic_changed: source_type for same IP responding with new MAC, confirmed over 2 detections (NIC_CONFIRM_COUNT), high if is_vital else medium; mac_history pushed; pending tracked in managed_devices.mac_change_pending (cleared on transient flip-back or when new MAC owned by another managed device). mac_rescue.start_mac_rescue returns None when mac_is_shared. Reference tests: /app/backend/tests/test_mac_follow_iter154.py (13 cases), /app/backend/tests/test_mac_rescue_iter159.py (3 cases). Both PASS. Prior iter157 test file test_mac_dup_repro.py referred to old merge semantics (NAS01 duplicate merge) which is REMOVED - do not re-run that file against current code without rewriting it.
rca of the issue: Not a bug fix iteration - verification of newly-adopted shared-MAC semantics. mac_is_shared returns True when count_documents on managed_devices with the same (case-insensitive) MAC > 1; apply_mac_follow short-circuits via `if len(group) > 1: continue` right after the nic_changed check, preventing any move/merge/alert for shared MACs while still allowing nic_changed detection per-IP. _resolve_shared_noise is invoked whenever any shared condition is observed in the current batch (shared_seen flag) to auto-close stale noise. mac_rescue.start_mac_rescue early-returns None on mac_is_shared, disabling vital rescue for VM-dense NICs where ARP cannot disambiguate which VM moved.
